model_output.score_comment_short: Class sizes, reading growth, and team leadership make the teaching work concrete.
model_output.score_comment_long: The current role includes a district assessment result and specific classroom and team responsibilities. The methods behind the reading result and contributions to the math pilot are less clear. Adding those details would make the work easier to understand.
model_output.score_plain: Your resume gives a reviewer concrete reasons to consider you for elementary teaching roles. A few examples of how you teach and contribute to school programs would help distinguish your approach.
model_output.first_impression: Your current role combines fourth-grade instruction with grade-level planning and a math curriculum pilot. The reading assessment result is worth keeping because it gives a reviewer a concrete view of student growth.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Served on the school's positive behavior support committee" doesn't explain what you contributed, leaving a reviewer unsure how you participated.
model_output.summary: Fourth-grade teaching is the center of this resume, with responsibility for all core subjects and a class that includes English language learners. You also lead weekly planning and data meetings for the grade-level team and trained other teachers on a new math curriculum. That combination points to an experienced classroom teacher with team-level responsibilities. The resume doesn't yet explain the instructional choices behind the reading growth, so a reviewer has less to go on when considering how you approach literacy instruction.
strengths: The class of 27 and the description of its English language learners help a reviewer picture your current classroom.
The family literacy night attendance of 140 families in 2019 shows the reach of an event you coordinated.
Your Washington K-8 certificate and English Language Learner endorsement make your qualifications easy to locate.
gaps: The math pilot doesn't describe what you tested or shared with colleagues, making your contribution to its rollout less specific.
Your work on the positive behavior support committee is named but not explained, so its connection to classroom practice is unclear.
The homework club lists its schedule and attendance but not the support you provide to students there.
